assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nasal cavity is lined with tiny hairs and sticky mucus that trap dust and other impurities from the air you inhale.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the filtering function of the human nasal cavity. G3-L-3 is about characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The card provides no information about growth, response, or reproduction, and is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nasal cavity is lined with tiny hairs and sticky mucus that trap dust and other impurities from the air you inhale.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-2 is about the root and shoot system in plants. The card is about the human nasal cavity, a part of the respiratory system, and has no connection to plant root or shoot systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nasal cavity is lined with tiny hairs and sticky mucus that trap dust and other impurities from the air you inhale.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: G3-L-5 is about observing the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) and their roles. The card discusses the human nasal cavity, not any plant part, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: The nasal cavity is lined with tiny hairs and sticky mucus that trap dust and other impurities from the air you inhale.
copy.tl: Ang nasal cavity ay may maliliit na buhok at malagkit na mucus na sumasalo ng alikabok at iba pang dumi mula sa hanging nilalanghap mo.
copy.bis: Ang nasal cavity adunay gagmay nga mga balhibo ug sticky mucus nga mosala sa abog ug uban pang hugaw sa hangin nga imong giginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Natality, or birth rate, and mortality, or death rate, are two factors that change population size.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses population dynamics (birth and death rates), which is unrelated to the particle model of matter, particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects described in G7-M-3.

copy.en: Natality, or birth rate, and mortality, or death rate, are two factors that change population size.
copy.tl: Ang natality, o birth rate, at mortality, o death rate, ay dalawang salik na nagpapabago sa laki ng population.
copy.bis: Ang natality, o birth rate, ug mortality, o death rate, maoy duha ka hinungdan nga nag-usab sa gidak-on sa population.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Of the 118 known elements, 92 are naturally occurring in the environment, while 26 are synthetic elements made in laboratories
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Element counts are unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 92 are naturally occurring in the environment, while 26 are synthetic elements made in laboratories
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Natural versus synthetic elements are unrelated to the five body systems.

copy.en: Of the 118 known elements, 92 are naturally occurring in the environment, while 26 are synthetic elements made in laboratories.
copy.tl: Sa 118 na element, 92 ang natural na makikita sa kapaligiran, habang 26 ang synthetic element na gawa sa laboratory.
copy.bis: Sa 118 ka element, 92 ang natural nga makita sa kinaiyahan, samtang 26 ang synthetic element nga gihimo sa laboratoryo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The natural greenhouse effect occurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the natural greenhouse effect (solar energy absorption and re-radiation by greenhouse gases). It has no content about life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The natural greenhouse effect occurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the greenhouse effect and atmospheric energy balance, not about the root and shoot system of plants. It provides no instructional support for observing or describing plant root/shoot systems.

copy.en: The natural greenhouse effect occurs when the Sun's energy enters the atmosphere, some is reflected to space, and the rest is absorbed and re-radiated by greenhouse gases.
copy.tl: Ang natural na greenhouse effect ay nangyayari kapag pumasok ang energy ng Araw sa atmosphere, ang ilan ay nire-reflect sa space, at ang iba ay ina-absorb at muling inilalabas ng greenhouse gases.
copy.bis: Ang natural nga greenhouse effect mahitabo kon mosulod ang energy sa Adlaw sa atmosphere, ang uban gi-reflect sa space, ug ang uban gi-absorb ug gipagawas pag-usab sa greenhouse gases.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Is a lake a natural or man-made source of water?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about classifying water sources as natural or man-made. It contains no content about assembling or drawing a simple circuit, batteries, wires, switches, bulbs, motors, or buzzers. The competency is entirely unrelated to the card.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A natural source of water because it forms on its own in nature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses natural versus man-made water sources. It does not address electricity as a flow of electrons, safe handling of electricity, or any related electrical concepts. The competency is unrelated to the card.

copy.en:
Is a lake a natural or man-made source of water?

A natural source of water because it forms on its own in nature, unlike a water pipe that people build.
copy.tl:
Ang lawa ba ay likas o gawa ng tao na pinagkukunan ng tubig?

Likas na pinagkukunan ng tubig dahil ito ay nabubuo nang mag-isa sa kalikasan, hindi tulad ng water pipe na itinayo ng mga tao.
copy.bis:
Ang lanaw ba natural o hinimo sa tao nga tinubdan sa tubig?

Natural nga tinubdan sa tubig tungod kay kini maporma nga mag-inusara sa kinaiyahan, dili sama sa water pipe nga gitukod sa mga tao.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an object is closer to a concave mirror than its focal point, the image formed is virtual, upright, and larger than the object.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different types of collisions as elastic or inelastic by providing some examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes image formation by a concave mirror, which is an optics topic. G10-F-2 concerns elastic and inelastic collisions; there is no instructional support for that competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an object is closer to a concave mirror than its focal point, the image formed is virtual, upright, and larger than the object.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes concave mirror image characteristics, not kinetic or potential energy. It does not support G8-F-4 in any substantive way.

copy.en: When an object is closer to a concave mirror than its focal point, the image formed is virtual, upright, and larger than the object.
copy.tl: Kapag ang bagay ay mas malapit sa concave mirror kaysa sa focal point nito, ang nabubuong imahe ay virtual, upright, at mas malaki kaysa sa bagay.
copy.bis: Kung ang butang mas duol sa concave mirror kaysa sa focal point, ang maporma nga imahe virtual, upright, ug mas dako kaysa sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep data neat and aligned in a table so it is easy to read and compare measurements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about organizing measurement data in a table, which is a general data-recording skill. It provides no information about ion formation, loss/gain of electrons, or ionic bonds as required by G9-M-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep data neat and aligned in a table so it is easy to read and compare measurements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses neat and aligned data tables for comparing measurements. It does not describe valence electrons, the outer shell, or bond formation, so it does not support G9-M-3.

copy.en: Keep data neat and aligned in a table so it is easy to read and compare measurements.
copy.tl: Panatilihing maayos at nakahanay ang data sa table para madaling basahin at ikumpara ang mga sukat.
copy.bis: Hupti nga hapsay ug naka-align ang data sa table aron sayon basahon ug ikumpara ang mga sukod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune and Uranus are called twin planets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the similarity of Neptune and Uranus as planets, which is unrelated to the competency 'explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals'. The card provides no information about soil formation, rocks, or minerals.

copy.en:
Which planet is Uranus's twin?

Neptune and Uranus are called twin planets because they have about the same color, size, and mass.
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang kambal ng Uranus?

Ang Neptune at Uranus ay tinatawag na twin planets dahil halos magkapareho ang kanilang kulay, laki, at mass.
copy.bis:
Hain nga planeta ang kaluha sa Uranus?

Ang Neptune ug Uranus gitawag nga twin planets tungod kay halos pareho sila ug kolor, gidak-on, ug mass.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nervous system regulates the speed at which food moves through the digestive tract.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: classify geological faults according to the angle of the fault plane and direction of slip
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the nervous system's role in digestion, which is a biology topic. G7-E-1 requires classifying geological faults by fault plane angle and slip direction, an earth science topic. There is no overlap in content.

copy.en: The nervous system regulates the speed at which food moves through the digestive tract.
copy.tl: Kinokontrol ng nervous system ang bilis ng paggalaw ng pagkain sa digestive tract.
copy.bis: Gikontrol sa nervous system ang katulin sa paglihok sa pagkaon sa digestive tract.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A net force, which is the total unbalanced force on an object, changes the object's state of motion or acceleration.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches net force and acceleration, a physics topic. G4-E-6 is about examining local weather charts and safety precautions for poor weather. No overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: A net force, which is the total unbalanced force on an object, changes the object's state of motion or acceleration.
copy.tl: Ang net force, na siyang kabuuang hindi balanseng puwersa sa isang bagay, ang nagbabago sa estado ng paggalaw o acceleration ng bagay.
copy.bis: Ang net force, nga mao ang kinatibuk-ang dili balanse nga puwersa sa usa ka butang, maoy mag-usab sa kahimtang sa paglihok o acceleration sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Volcanic eruptions can create new land when lava hardens into domes, plateaus, and even entire volcanic mountains
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Volcanic landforms are unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

copy.en: Volcanic eruptions can create new land when lava hardens into domes, plateaus, and even entire volcanic mountains.
copy.tl: Ang pagputok ng bulkan ay nakakalikha ng bagong lupa kapag tumigas ang lava at naging mga dome, talampas, at maging buong bundok na bulkan.
copy.bis: Ang pagbuto sa bulkan makahimo og bag-ong yuta kung mogahi ang lava ug mahimong mga dome, plateau, ug bisan tibuok nga bukid nga bulkan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical change is a change in which at least one new substance forms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines chemical change and gives an example (banana turning brown). The competency G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions). The card does not mention mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, and instead addresses a different concept (chemical change).

copy.en: A chemical change is a change in which at least one new substance forms, like a banana turning brown.
copy.tl: Ang chemical change ay pagbabago kung saan may nabubuong kahit isang bagong substance, tulad ng saging na nagiging kulay brown.
copy.bis: Ang chemical change usa ka pagbag-o diin adunay mahimong labing menos usa ka bag-ong substance, sama sa saging nga nahimong brown.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are nine major lithospheric plates on Earth, and the Pacific Plate is the largest of them all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Lithospheric plates are unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are nine major lithospheric plates on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Plates are unrelated to identifying nose, windpipe, and lungs.

copy.en: There are nine major lithospheric plates on Earth, and the Pacific Plate is the largest of them all.
copy.tl: Mayroong siyam na major lithospheric plates sa Earth, at ang Pacific Plate ang pinakamalaki sa kanilang lahat.
copy.bis: Adunay siyam ka major lithospheric plates sa Earth, ug ang Pacific Plate mao ang kinadak-an nilang tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: density generally increases with atomic mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density trends in the nitrogen group (chemistry), which has no connection to simple machines, inclined planes, wedges, levers, or pulleys. The competency is about demonstrating advantages and limitations of simple machines through guided investigation.

copy.en: In the nitrogen group, density generally increases with atomic mass, from nitrogen's very low density to bismuth's much higher density.
copy.tl: Sa nitrogen group, tumataas ang density habang tumataas ang atomic mass, mula sa napakababang density ng nitrogen hanggang sa mas mataas na density ng bismuth.
copy.bis: Sa nitrogen group, motaas ang density samtang motaas ang atomic mass, gikan sa ubos kaayo nga density sa nitrogen hangtod sa mas taas nga density sa bismuth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Non-living things cannot reproduce
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses reproduction of non-living things, which is unrelated to identifying community issues and how science addresses them (e.g., waste treatment).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Non-living things cannot reproduce
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reproduction, not chemical properties such as burning, reactivity, or biodegradability.

copy.en: Non-living things cannot reproduce, so a rock can never make a baby rock, and water can never make new water on its own.
copy.tl: Ang mga non-living thing ay hindi maaaring magparami, kaya ang isang bato ay hindi kailanman makakagawa ng batang bato, at ang tubig ay hindi kailanman makakagawa ng bagong tubig nang mag-isa.
copy.bis: Ang mga non-living thing dili makapasanay, mao nga ang usa ka bato dili gyud makahimo og batang bato, ug ang tubig dili gyud makahimo og bag-ong tubig nga siya ra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Asexual reproduction does not allow genetic variation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses asexual reproduction and genetic variation, which is unrelated to the G4-L-1 competency about describing how human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. No part of the card supports this competency.

copy.en: Asexual reproduction does not allow genetic variation, but it guarantees reproduction because the organism does not depend on finding a mate.
copy.tl: Ang asexual reproduction ay hindi nagpapahintulot ng genetic variation, ngunit tinitiyak nito ang pagpaparami dahil hindi umaasa ang organismo sa paghahanap ng kapareha.
copy.bis: Ang asexual reproduction dili motugot og genetic variation, apan gigarantiyahan niini ang pagsanay tungod kay ang organismo dili magsalig sa pagpangita og pares.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In non-conservative collisions, mechanical energy is dissipated as heat, sound, or permanent deformation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy dissipation in non-conservative collisions, which is a physics concept about collisions and mechanical energy. G4-F-4 requires constructing and labeling simple speed-time graphs (stationary and uniform speeds). The card provides no information about graphing speeds or motion graphs, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: In non-conservative collisions, mechanical energy is dissipated as heat, sound, or permanent deformation, so the total motion energy after is less than before.
copy.tl: Sa non-conservative collision, ang mechanical energy ay nawawala bilang init, tunog, o permanenteng pagka-deform, kaya mas kaunti ang kabuuang motion energy pagkatapos kaysa bago.
copy.bis: Sa non-conservative collision, ang mechanical energy mawala isip init, tingog, o permanenteng pagkadeform, busa mas gamay ang kinatibuk-ang motion energy pagkahuman kaysa sa wala pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Non-porous materials do not let air or liquid pass through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes material porosity and water protection, not momentum, mass, velocity, or collision impact. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Non-porous materials do not let air or liquid pass through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish between speed and velocity using the concept of vectors
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about non-porous materials and plastic covers, not speed, velocity, or vectors. Completely unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Non-porous materials do not allow water to pass through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a material property (non-porosity and water absorption) and has no connection to kinetic energy, potential energy, or their transformation, which is the sole subject of G8-F-5.

copy.en: Non-porous materials do not allow water to pass through, so they do not absorb water.
copy.tl: Ang mga non-porous na materyal ay hindi pinapadaan ang tubig, kaya hindi sila nag-a-absorb ng tubig.
copy.bis: Ang mga non-porous nga materyal dili makapaagi sa tubig, mao nga dili sila mo-absorb ug tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nonmetal items such as erasers and paper bills do not complete a circuit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical conductivity of nonmetals in a circuit, which is a physics/electricity topic. G9-L-5 concerns biodiversity and ecosystem stability, which is unrelated to the card's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nonmetal items such as erasers and paper bills do not complete a circuit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about nonmetals blocking electric current, not about biotic/abiotic factors in an ecosystem. G6-L-7 is a living-things/ecology competency, so the card does not support it at all.

copy.en: Nonmetal items such as erasers and paper bills do not complete a circuit, so the bulb stays dark when they are in the path.
copy.tl: Ang mga bagay na hindi metal tulad ng erasers at paper bills ay hindi kumukumpleto ng circuit, kaya nananatiling madilim ang bulb kapag sila ang nasa daanan.
copy.bis: Ang mga butang nga dili metal sama sa erasers ug paper bills dili makakompleto sa circuit, mao nga magpabilin nga ngitngit ang bulb kung sila ang naa sa agianan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The normal force is the upward push from a surface that supports an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the physics concept of normal force (a contact force from a surface). G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions, suspensions). There is no overlap in subject matter; the card does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en: The normal force is the support force from a surface, like a table pushing up on a book, and it always acts perpendicular to the surface.
copy.tl: Ang normal force ay ang support force mula sa isang surface, tulad ng mesa na tumutulak paitaas sa libro, at ito ay laging kumikilos nang perpendicular sa surface.
copy.bis: Ang normal force mao ang support force gikan sa usa ka surface, sama sa lamesa nga nagtulod paitaas sa libro, ug kini kanunay molihok nga perpendicular sa surface.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Protons and neutrons are together called nucleons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the composition of an atomic nucleus (protons and neutrons as nucleons), which is a chemistry/atomic structure topic. The competency G10-L-2 requires explaining how homeostasis is maintained through positive and negative feedback mechanisms, a biology topic. There is no instructional support for homeostasis or feedback mechanisms.

copy.en: Protons and neutrons are together called nucleons because they are the two particles that make up the nucleus of an atom.
copy.tl: Ang mga proton at neutron ay magkasamang tinatawag na nucleons dahil sila ang dalawang particle na bumubuo sa nucleus ng isang atom.
copy.bis: Ang mga proton ug neutron gitawag nga nucleons tungod kay sila ang duha ka particle nga naglangkob sa nucleus sa usa ka atom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a nerve gets pressed or blocked, that part of the body can go numb
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains nerve blockage causing numbness, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a nerve gets pressed or blocked, that part of the body can go numb
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a labelled diagram or describe levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere; it only gives a simple explanation of numbness from nerve blockage.

copy.en:
Why does a body part go numb sometimes?

When a nerve gets pressed or blocked, that part of the body can go numb and briefly lose its feeling.
copy.tl:
Bakit namamanhid ang bahagi ng katawan minsan?

Kapag naipit o nahaharangan ang nerbiyo, maaaring mamanhid ang bahaging iyon ng katawan at pansamantalang mawala ang pakiramdam nito.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga manhid usahay ang bahin sa lawas?

Kung maipit o ma-block ang nerbiyo, mahimong manhid kanang bahin sa lawas ug temporaryo mawad-an og bati.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nutrition labels on food packages can be analyzed to find the percent by mass of protein, fats, and carbohydrates in a serving.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate and describe the relationship among the projectile variables including the angle and velocity of release, and projectile height and range, using everyday activities such as shooting basketballs or kicking footballs
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses analyzing nutrition labels for percent by mass of macronutrients, which is unrelated to projectile motion variables (angle, velocity, height, range). No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Nutrition labels on food packages can be analyzed to find the percent by mass of protein, fats, and carbohydrates in a serving.
copy.tl: Ang mga nutrition label sa pakete ng pagkain ay maaaring suriin upang malaman ang percent by mass ng protein, fats, at carbohydrates sa isang serving.
copy.bis: Ang mga nutrition label sa pakete sa pagkaon mahimong analisahon aron mahibaloan ang percent by mass sa protein, fats, ug carbohydrates sa usa ka serving.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the concave lens still forms an erect, virtual, and reduced image
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes image formation by a concave lens, which is a topic in geometric optics. G9-F-11 requires comparing wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves (radio, microwave, infrared, etc.). The card provides no information about electromagnetic wave types, wavelengths, or frequencies, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: When the object is placed between the lens and its focus, the concave lens still forms an erect, virtual, and reduced image in that same small space.
copy.tl: Kapag ang object ay inilagay sa pagitan ng lens at ng focus nito, ang concave lens ay bumubuo pa rin ng erect, virtual, at pinaliit na image sa maliit na espasyong iyon.
copy.bis: Kon ang object ibutang tali sa lens ug sa focus niini, ang concave lens moporma gihapon og erect, virtual, ug gamay nga image sa maong gamay nga luna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iron filings, thumb tacks, staple wire, pins, coins, and needles are common objects that are attracted to a magnet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about objects attracted to magnets, which is a magnetism/physics topic. It provides no information about comets, meteoroids, asteroids, or dwarf planets, nor about how they help understand Earth and Solar System formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iron filings, thumb tacks, staple wire, pins, coins, and needles are common objects that are attracted to a magnet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about magnetic attraction of common objects and has no connection to the geologic time scale or recounting Earth's history.

copy.en: Iron filings, thumb tacks, staple wire, pins, coins, and needles are common objects that are attracted to a magnet.
copy.tl: Ang iron filings, thumb tacks, staple wire, pins, coins, at needles ay mga karaniwang bagay na naaakit ng magnet.
copy.bis: Ang iron filings, thumb tacks, staple wire, pins, coins, ug dagom mao ang kasagarang mga butang nga ma-attract sa magnet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you use your senses to note its properties, like its white color and waxy texture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes observing a candle's physical properties. It has no connection to local impacts of global climate change or ways to reduce global warming.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you use your senses to note its properties, like its white color and waxy texture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sensory observation of a candle, not about identifying evidence of global warming or climate change.

copy.en: When you observe a candle, you use your senses to note its properties, like its white color and waxy texture.
copy.tl: Kapag nag-oobserve ka ng kandila, ginagamit mo ang iyong mga pandama upang pansinin ang mga katangian nito, tulad ng puting kulay at waxy na tekstura.
copy.bis: Kung mag-obserbar ka og kandila, gamiton nimo ang imong mga panimati aron matikdan ang mga kinaiya niini, sama sa puti nga kolor ug waxy nga tekstura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Observing means using your senses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to describe and explain what mechanisms that drive the movement of tectonic plates including the role of the asthenosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the meaning of observation using senses in science. It has no content about tectonic plate movement mechanisms or the asthenosphere, which is the subject of G10-E-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Observing means using your senses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the general skill of observing with senses, not about structures, movements, or events at plate boundaries. It does not support G10-E-2 in any way.

copy.en:
What does it mean to observe in science?

Observing means using your senses - sight, hearing, smell, touch, and taste - to describe facts about the world around you.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng pag-oobserve sa science?

Ang pag-oobserve ay paggamit ng iyong senses - paningin, pandinig, pang-amoy, pandama, at panlasa - para ilarawan ang mga katotohanan sa iyong paligid.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa pag-observe sa science?

Ang pag-observe mao ang paggamit sa imong senses - panan-aw, pandungog, pagpanimaho, paghikap, ug pagtilaw - aron ihulagway ang mga kamatuoran sa imong palibut.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Harry Hess discovered that the seafloor was not smooth but full of canyons, trenches, and volcanic sea mountains.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Harry Hess's discovery of ocean floor features (canyons, trenches, volcanic sea mountains). It has no content about inertia, rest, motion, or unbalanced net force. The competency is a physics/Newton's laws topic, while the card is geological/oceanographic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Harry Hess discovered that the seafloor was not smooth but full of canyons, trenches, and volcanic sea mountains.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses seafloor topography, not the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass. It provides no instructional support for this physics competency.

copy.en: Harry Hess discovered that the seafloor was not smooth but full of canyons, trenches, and volcanic sea mountains.
copy.tl: Natuklasan ni Harry Hess na ang seafloor ay hindi patag kundi puno ng mga canyon, trench, at volcanic sea mountains.
copy.bis: Nadiskobrehan ni Harry Hess nga ang seafloor dili patag kondili puno sa mga canyon, trench, ug volcanic sea mountains.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Odor is the smell of a compound, and every organic compound has its own specific odor
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: Compound odor is chemistry, not rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: from the strong smell of gasoline to the sour smell of vinegar
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Organic-compound odor is unrelated to how plants reproduce.

copy.en: Odor is the smell of a compound, and every organic compound has its own specific odor, from the strong smell of gasoline to the sour smell of vinegar.
copy.tl: Ang odor ay ang amoy ng isang compound, at bawat organic compound ay may sarili nitong partikular na amoy, mula sa malakas na amoy ng gasoline hanggang sa maasim na amoy ng suka.
copy.bis: Ang odor mao ang baho sa usa ka compound, ug ang matag organic compound adunay kaugalingong partikular nga baho, gikan sa kusog nga baho sa gasoline hangtod sa aslom nga baho sa suka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil immersion objectives, marked 97x or 100x, are used to view bacteria, very small protists, and fungi.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a microscope objective lens used to view tiny organisms. G5-E-12 requires making drawings or a model of Earth-Moon-Sun motion to explain moon phases. There is no connection to astronomy, moon phases, or Earth-Moon-Sun motion.

copy.en: Oil immersion objectives, marked 97x or 100x, are used to view bacteria, very small protists, and fungi.
copy.tl: Ang oil immersion objectives, na may markang 97x o 100x, ay ginagamit para makita ang bacteria, napakaliit na protists, at fungi.
copy.bis: Ang oil immersion objectives, nga adunay marka nga 97x o 100x, gigamit aron makita ang bacteria, gagmay kaayo nga protists, ug fungi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A one-degree global temperature change requires enormous heat and can significantly affect climate.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses global warming, heat, and climate change. It contains no information about wave properties, amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, nor any research using secondary sources. The topic is entirely unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A one-degree global temperature change requires enormous heat and can significantly affect climate.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about global temperature change and climate, not about how sound is made or transferred. There is no mention of sound, ringing bells, hearing noises, or any everyday sound situation. The competency is not supported at all.

copy.en:
Why care about one degree of global warming?

A one-degree global temperature change requires enormous heat and can significantly affect climate.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat alalahanin ang isang degree ng global warming?

Ang isang degree na pagbabago sa global temperature ay nangangailangan ng napakalaking init at malaki ang epekto sa klima.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga angay kabalak-an ang usa ka degree nga global warming?

Ang usa ka degree nga pagbag-o sa global temperature nagkinahanglan ug hilabihan ka daghan nga init ug dako ang epekto sa klima.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An organism is any single living thing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model)
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an organism as a single living thing made of organ systems. It contains no information about metals, metallic bonding, or the sea of electrons model, so it does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: An organism is any single living thing that can survive on its own, like one dog, one mango tree, or one person, made of all the organ systems working together.
copy.tl: Ang organism ay kahit anong isang buhay na bagay na kayang mabuhay mag-isa, tulad ng isang aso, isang puno ng mangga, o isang tao, na binubuo ng lahat ng organ systems na nagtutulungan.
copy.bis: Ang organism mao ang bisan unsang usa ka buhing butang nga makalahutay sa iyang kaugalingon, sama sa usa ka iro, usa ka punoan sa mangga, o usa ka tawo, nga gilangkuban sa tanang organ systems nga nagtinabangay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gymnosperm seeds like pine nuts often lack endosperm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses seed anatomy (cotyledons, endosperm) in gymnosperms vs angiosperms. It has no content about changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or diagrams/flowcharts of those processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gymnosperm seeds like pine nuts often lack endosperm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant seed structure, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). No relevant instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Do pine seeds have the same parts as bean seeds?

Not exactly! Gymnosperm seeds like pine nuts often lack endosperm and have only one cotyledon, unlike the two cotyledons in many angiosperm seeds.
copy.tl:
Pareho ba ang mga parte ng buto ng pine sa buto ng bean?

Hindi eksakto! Ang mga buto ng gymnosperm tulad ng pine nuts ay kadalasang walang endosperm at may isang cotyledon lamang, hindi tulad ng dalawang cotyledon sa maraming buto ng angiosperm.
copy.bis:
Pareho ba ang mga parte sa liso sa pine ug sa liso sa bean?

Dili eksakto! Ang mga liso sa gymnosperm sama sa pine nuts kasagarang walay endosperm ug adunay usa lang ka cotyledon, dili sama sa duha ka cotyledon sa daghang liso sa angiosperm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One complete wave cycle includes one crest and one trough
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a wave cycle (crest and trough), which is a physics/waves concept. G9-E-9 is about distinguishing comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets and their role in understanding the solar system. No connection to wave cycles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One complete wave cycle includes one crest and one trough
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about wave cycles, not the structure of the solar system or celestial objects. G5-E-11 requires describing the solar system's general structure, major celestial objects, features, and composition. The card provides no such information.

copy.en: One complete wave cycle includes one crest and one trough - after that, the wave pattern repeats itself exactly.
copy.tl: Ang isang kumpletong cycle ng wave ay may kasamang isang crest at isang trough - pagkatapos nito, eksaktong umuulit ang pattern ng wave.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka kompleto nga cycle sa wave naglakip og usa ka crest ug usa ka trough - pagkahuman niana, eksakto nga mobalik ang pattern sa wave.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Open-mindedness is a scientific attitude that means listening to other people's ideas and being willing to change your mind when new evidence appears.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines open-mindedness as a scientific attitude. G5-M-6 requires describing how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). The card provides no information about matter, temperature, or phase changes, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: Open-mindedness is a scientific attitude that means listening to other people's ideas and being willing to change your mind when new evidence appears.
copy.tl: Ang open-mindedness ay isang scientific attitude na nangangahulugang pakikinig sa ideya ng iba at pagiging handang magbago ng isip kapag may bagong ebidensya.
copy.bis: Ang open-mindedness usa ka scientific attitude nga nagpasabot sa pagpaminaw sa mga ideya sa uban ug pagkaandam nga mag-usab sa hunahuna kon adunay bag-ong ebidensya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When two objects have opposite charges, one negative and one positive, they pull toward each other with an invisible force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Opposite electric charges are unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they pull toward each other with an invisible force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: Charge attraction is not a labelled diagram of levels of organization from cells to the biosphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they pull toward each other with an invisible force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: Charge attraction is not models of digestion and excretion.

copy.en: When two objects have opposite charges, one negative and one positive, they pull toward each other with an invisible force.
copy.tl: Kapag ang dalawang bagay ay may magkaibang charge, isang negative at isang positive, humihila sila papunta sa isa't isa gamit ang isang hindi nakikitang puwersa.
copy.bis: Kung ang duha ka butang adunay magkaatbang nga charge, usa ka negative ug usa ka positive, mobira sila padulong sa usag usa gamit ang dili makitang puwersa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When Earth's orbit becomes more elongated, Earth moves closer to the Sun and temperatures become higher than usual.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses orbital eccentricity and its effect on Earth's temperature, which is an astronomy/earth science topic. It provides no information about separating mixtures (decantation, winnowing, filtering, etc.) as required by G6-M-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When Earth's orbit becomes more elongated, Earth moves closer to the Sun and temperatures become higher than usual.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain benefits of mixture separation techniques in preparing useful products. It is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: When Earth's orbit becomes more elongated, Earth moves closer to the Sun and temperatures become higher than usual.
copy.tl: Kapag ang orbit ng Earth ay naging mas elongated, lumalapit ang Earth sa Araw at tumataas ang temperatura kaysa karaniwan.
copy.bis: Kung ang orbit sa Earth mahimong mas elongated, ang Earth moduol sa Adlaw ug motaas ang temperatura kaysa naandan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Arranged from longest to shortest wavelength, the colors are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the order of visible light colors by wavelength, a physics/light topic. G6-E-8 requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to explain seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. There is no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Arranged from longest to shortest wavelength, the colors are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
copy.tl: Kung isasaayos mula sa pinakamahaba hanggang sa pinakamaikling wavelength, ang mga kulay ay red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, at violet.
copy.bis: Kon ihan-ay gikan sa pinakataas hangtod sa pinakamubo nga wavelength, ang mga kolor mao ang red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, ug violet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A data table is a way to organize numerical data in rows and columns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to organize numerical data in a table, which is a general data-handling skill. It provides no information about the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun, the phases of the moon, or any Earth/space content required by G5-E-12.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After an experiment, scientists organize and interpret data
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes organizing and interpreting experimental data, which is a general science process skill. G7-M-4 requires using diagrams/illustrations to describe particle arrangement, spacing, and motion in the three states of matter. The card provides no information about the particle model or states of matter, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: After an experiment, scientists organize and interpret data by recording what they observed and looking for patterns that explain what happened.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng experiment, inaayos at iniinterpret ng mga scientist ang data sa pamamagitan ng pagtatala ng kanilang naobserbahan at paghahanap ng mga pattern na nagpapaliwanag sa nangyari.
copy.bis: Human sa experiment, gi-organize ug gi-interpret sa mga scientist ang data pinaagi sa pagsulat sa ilang na-obserbahan ug pagpangita og mga pattern nga nagpasabot sa nahitabo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An organ system is a group of organs that work as a team, like the circulatory system using the heart and blood vessels to move blood.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about organ systems and how organs work together, which is a biology/living-things topic. G3-F-2 concerns forces affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). There is no connection to movement of objects or forces.

copy.en:
Why can't one organ do everything alone?

Because most jobs in the body need many organs working together! An organ system is a group of organs that work as a team, like the circulatory system using the heart and blood vessels to move blood.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi kayang gawin ng isang organ ang lahat nang mag-isa?

Dahil karamihan ng trabaho sa katawan ay nangangailangan ng maraming organ na nagtutulungan! Ang organ system ay grupo ng mga organ na nagtutulungan bilang team, tulad ng circulatory system na gumagamit ng puso at mga daluyan ng dugo para ilipat ang dugo.
copy.bis:
Ngano man nga dili mahimo sa usa ka organ ang tanan nga mag-inusara?

Tungod kay kadaghanan sa trabaho sa lawas nagkinahanglan ug daghang organ nga magtinabangay! Ang organ system mao ang grupo sa mga organ nga magtinabangay isip team, sama sa circulatory system nga mogamit sa kasingkasing ug mga ugat sa dugo aron molihok ang dugo.
